purpose: Cross-platform session handoff and task queue. Read at the start of every session. Update at the end of every session that makes meaningful changes. Either platform can suspend any task mid-flight and the other can resume it.

on_session_start: 2. The explicit current user request has precedence. Otherwise check active_task and resume it only when its next_action is executable and resume_by has not expired.
3. Run `python3 tools/session_queue_health.py --summary`; select ready work by priority and review_at. Waiting/parked work is considered only when its trigger or review_at is due.
4. Check tool_versions for any tools installed since you last worked here.
5. Run `git log --oneline -5` to see what landed since last_updated.
on_session_end: 1. End every active task with an explicit transition: complete-active, suspend-active with resume_by, wait-active with a concrete trigger, or park-active with a review date.
3. Append new commits to recent_commits (keep last 10).
4. Update tool_versions if anything was installed.
6. Push to origin so the other platform sees it.
protocol.suspend_rule: Suspended means immediately resumable work, never an indefinite owner/future gate. A suspend point must be self-contained, have an executable next_action and resume_by, and require only this file plus context_files to continue.
protocol.owner_gate_rule: Routine reversible investigation, diagnosis, tests, local edits, and draft/PR preparation proceed without an owner gate. Owner approval is reserved for concrete consequential decisions that meet catalog/session_queue_policy.json requirements.
protocol.conflict_rule: If both platforms made commits since last_updated, merge recent_commits by date. Do not overwrite — append.

strengths: Precise multi-file editing with Read/Edit/Write tools
Static analysis: Codacy (Agentlinter, Ruff, Bandit, Semgrep), gitleaks

Aurora governance skills (canon-reconciler, governance-orchestrator, script-governor, narrative-tone-governor, repo-stabilizer, threadcore, zipwiz)
limitations: Less precise on multi-file surgical edits
